papers.title_en: MRFlow: Mechanism-Structured Residual Flow Matching for Virtual Cell Perturbation Prediction
papers.evidence: 通过条件流匹配预测单细胞对化学与遗传扰动的转录响应
papers.tldr: 单细胞扰动预测常被简化为平均表达偏移，忽略了稀有状态、耐药亚群和情境依赖的效应。MRFlow 将虚拟细胞预测建模为控制细胞群到扰动细胞群的条件传输，在变分潜空间中用条件流匹配向量场完成搬运。该向量场分解为机制结构仿射字典与谱控残差场，遗传和化学扰动分别经调控图GCN和Morgan指纹编码，并共享同一条件动力学接口。在八个基因与药物扰动基准上，MRFlow 取得最高综合得分，同时保持有竞争力的差异表达与分布指标。
papers.abstract_en: Predicting cellular responses to chemical and genetic perturbations is a central test for AI virtual cells, yet many single-cell models reduce each condition to an average expression shift. This target is misaligned with perturbation biology: rare states, resistant subpopulations, and context-dependent effect sizes may coexist under the same intervention. MRFlow treats virtual-cell prediction as conditional transport between empirical single-cell measures. Control and perturbed cells are embedded in a variational latent state space, greedy low-cost supervision is constructed over detached minibatch states, and a conditional flow-matching vector field transports control populations toward perturbed populations. The field decomposes into a mechanism-structured affine dictionary, which recombines shared latent response operators with a low-rank condition-specific correction, and a spectrally controlled residual field for nonlinear cell-level variation. Genetic perturbations are encoded through a regulatory-graph GCN, chemical perturbations through Morgan fingerprints, and both enter the same conditional dynamics interface. Across eight gene and drug perturbation benchmarks, MRFlow attains the highest composite score while preserving competitive raw performance on differential-expression and distributional metrics. The results support latent distribution transport as a principled and empirically effective formulation for perturbation-aware virtual cell modeling.

papers.title_en: PopPert: Population-level Joint-Distribution Modeling for Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction
papers.authors: Handong Wang, Jiaxin Qi, Haochen Feng, Baisheng Lai
papers.evidence: 面向单细胞扰动转录响应的群体级联合分布建模
papers.tldr: 单细胞扰动预测需从无配对对照与扰动群体推断转录响应，现有单细胞级方法依赖细胞对应关系，与数据实际不匹配。PopPert显式建模群体级联合基因表达分布，用低秩高斯Copula刻画跨基因依赖，并预测扰动引起的分布参数变化。在遗传与化学扰动基准上，其在差异表达恢复、扰动效应估计和群体分布匹配上整体优于现有方法。该工作将群体级联合分布学习确立为无配对单细胞扰动预测的有效范式。
papers.abstract_en: Predicting transcriptional responses to specific perturbations is critical for understanding cellular regulatory mechanisms and accelerating drug discovery. Single-cell RNA sequencing destroys each measured cell, yielding only unpaired populations of control and perturbed cells. However, existing methods typically model perturbation prediction at the single-cell level and assume cell-to-cell correspondence, which conflicts with the unpaired nature of the observed data. To address this challenge, we propose PopPert, a framework that explicitly parameterizes population-level joint gene expression distributions for collective transcriptional state modeling. Given a control population distribution and a perturbation condition, PopPert predicts perturbation-induced changes in distribution parameters, eliminating the need for cell-level correspondence and reducing sensitivity to single-cell noise. To effectively capture gene co-expression patterns, PopPert leverages a low-rank Gaussian Copula to model cross-gene statistical dependencies and construct the joint gene expression distribution, additionally allowing sampling of synthetic perturbed single-cell profiles. Across multiple single-cell benchmarks spanning both genetic and chemical perturbations, PopPert achieves superior overall performance in differential expression recovery, perturbation effect estimation, and population-level distribution matching. These results establish population-level joint distribution learning as an effective paradigm for predicting transcriptional responses from unpaired single-cell populations. Code for PopPert is publicly available at https://github.com/whd1125/PopPert.

papers.title_en: CellRFT: Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Single-Cell Perturbation Modeling
papers.authors: Jie Yan, Li Liu, Hanze Guo, Jiaxin Hu, Houxin He, Xiaoning Qi, Haoran Wang, Cong Li, Zhong-Yuan Zhang, Yong Wang
papers.evidence: 以生物学评价为直接训练反馈的单细胞扰动模型强化微调
papers.tldr: 单细胞扰动预测常以替代损失训练，数据拟合更好未必带来更优生物学预测。CellRFT将生物学评价作为直接反馈，用策略梯度优化生成细胞群体，并以分层奖励聚合整合多种生物奖励。实验显示其可跨预训练模型提升扰动预测，并揭示不同生物指标间存在促进或冲突。该框架为按生物评价塑造模型行为、反哺评测设计提供了新途径。
papers.abstract_en: Predicting cellular responses to perturbations supports the study of gene function, disease mechanisms, and therapeutic strategies. Despite advances in single-cell perturbation modeling, existing models typically optimize surrogate losses that do not directly reflect the biological criteria used for evaluation, so better data fitting need not yield better biological predictions. To address this mismatch, we introduce \textbf{CellRFT}, a reinforcement fine-tuning framework that uses biological evaluation as direct training feedback. CellRFT uses policy-gradient optimization to learn from non-differentiable evaluations of generated cell populations and integrates multiple biological rewards through hierarchical reward aggregation. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate CellRFT's applicability across different pretrained models and effectiveness in improving perturbation prediction, reveal that optimizing one biological criterion can help or hinder others, and show that complementary rewards can improve criteria beyond those directly optimized, offering a way to probe how biological metrics shape model behavior, with the potential to inform evaluation design. Code will be made available.

papers.title_en: scDEFT: A deep learning framework for drug-effect prediction and counterfactual reasoning
papers.evidence: 单细胞药物效应预测与反事实推理
papers.tldr: 纵向单细胞图谱可匹配同一药物下应答者与无应答者的治疗前后状态，但难以解释疗效差异。scDEFT 将药物视为细胞表示的条件算子，用特征级线性调制生成药物条件潜变量，并以两个独立头在共享转录邻域聚合，预测药物诱导状态变化和应答状态。在 116 万细胞、三个队列、两类药物的 IBD 图谱上，状态变化预测达到基线到可重复性上限间 45% 的余量，治疗前分层 AUROC 0.70。该框架支持靶点/共靶点提名、患者分层和未见药物队列效应的反事实预测。
papers.abstract_en: Longitudinal single cell atlases now capture matched pre treatment and post treatment states from responders and non responders, presenting an opportunity to mechanistically explain why two patients on the same drug diverge. We introduce scDEFT (single cell Drug EFfect Transducer), which treats a drug as a conditioning operator on cell representations, enabling prediction and explanation. In scDEFT, feature wise linear modulation produces drug conditioned cell latents, learned under abundant per cell supervision and then frozen. Two independent heads aggregate those latents over shared transcriptional neighborhoods to predict drug induced state change and responder status. A backward stage ranks the latent dimensions by how strongly they separate responders from non responders and maps them to genes under a cell composition control. On a harmonized inflammatory bowel disease atlas of 1.16 million cells, three cohorts and two drug classes, scDEFT predicts state change at 45% of the baseline to reproducibility ceiling headroom and stratifies responders before treatment at AUROC 0.70, where standard predictors remain at chance. These predictions and the drivers behind them support target and co target nomination, patient stratification, and counterfactual prediction of unseen drug cohort effects.

papers.title_en: Towards a knowledge-enhanced single-cell foundation model
papers.authors: Hanqing Zhang, Jie Bao, Mei Ma, Shuai Liu, Jiaying Ma, Jiaguan Liu, Jiaxiao Li, Zhenbo Li, Wenwen Gong, Zhijun Ca
papers.evidence: 注入基因调控与细胞注释监督的知识增强单细胞基础模型
papers.tldr: 单细胞基础模型依赖大规模转录组预训练，但继续扩数据收益递减且计算成本高。作者的数据缩放分析发现，细胞文本注释与基因调控信息可提供数据量之外的额外缩放维度。据此提出scKITE，用轻量辅助解码器在预训练中注入细胞注释和基因调控监督，预训练后丢弃解码器保留通用编码器。仅用17.9万样本、不足既往强模型0.5%，却在多下游任务超越，表明知识增强预训练是构建具生物学基础scFM的有前景范式。
papers.abstract_en: Single-cell foundation models (scFMs) increasingly rely on large-scale transcriptomic pretraining, yet expanding pretraining data can yield diminishing gains while substantially increasing computational cost. Our data scaling analyses showed that incorporating biological knowledge, including cell-level text annotation and gene-level regulatory information, provided additional scaling dimension than simply increasing data size. Motivated by this observation, we present scKITE, a simple yet effective scFM that integrates cell-annotation and gene-regulatory supervision into a shared transcriptomic Transformer encoder through lightweight auxiliary decoders. These decoders are used only during pretraining and subsequently discarded, yielding a general-purpose encoder enriched with biological knowledge for downstream applications. With only 179,067 pretraining samples, i.e., less than 0.5\% of those used by previous strong scFMs, scKITE outperformed these models across diverse downstream tasks, highlighting knowledge-enhanced pretraining as a promising paradigm for biologically grounded scFMs.
